newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia minister in Australia cash case unsighted.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia minister in Australia cash case unsighted.

text.p: Aides of a senior Malaysian politician charged with trying to take money out of Australia without approval said on Tuesday they could not locate him, and the opposition demanded his resignation over the affair.
"How are we to answer your queries. We can't even find him ourselves," an aide of Muhammad Muhammad Taib, chief minister of Malaysia's central Selangor state, told Reuters.

Muhammad was arrested at the Brisbane airport on Sunday and charged in a local court with trying to take an equivalent of A$1.2 million ($960,000) in Malaysian, Singaporean and New Zealand dollars out of Australia without approval.
Under Australian law, people leaving the country must declare and justify any amount worth over A$5,000 taken out, in whatever currency.
Muhammad's aides said his office had been inundated with telephone calls on Tuesday from friends and colleagues in Malaysia who had learnt of the charge against him.
"Frankly, all I know is that he's on holiday," said the aide, who declined to be named.
Some political sources said they believed Muhammad was back in the country, but this could not be confirmed.

The government did not immediately react to the charge against Muhammad and officials could not be contacted for a response. But opposition leader Lim Kit Siang demanded that Muhammad resign from his post to protect Malaysia's "good name".

"He should also explain how and why he was in possession of (nearly) 2.5 millon ringgit ($1 million) in various currency, whether he had taken this vast sum of money with him to Australia from Malaysia, or whether he had this money only when he was in Australia," Lim said in a statement.
Australian police said Muhammad, who arrived in Australia on December 16 on a "private business visit," was about to board a flight to New Zealand when the money was found.
He was released on unconditional bail and has to appear for a hearing on March 21.
Muhammad is a vice-president of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's United Malays National Organisation, Malaysia's dominant political party.
